subject: Notification: Elevated Auth Failure — Evidence & SIG follow-up
messages:
From: security@finplatform.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Elevated auth failures seen against service account svc-ingest-prod

Hi Sean,

We observed a spike in authentication failures and anomalous token refresh activity originating from one of your service principals that integrates with our ingestion pipeline (svc-ingest-prod). We classified it as an elevated-risk event and have temporarily throttled the integration while we investigate.

Can your team confirm whether this was expected (a rollout or key rotation) or if you need us to keep the integration disabled? Also, we will need a copy of your incident response plan for regulatory review and any relevant access logs for the timeframe 2026-06-14 22:00 UTC — 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC.

Requesting:
- brief incident statement
- list of affected service accounts
- access logs (CSV) and a summary timeline
- SOC 2 / SIG artifacts that demonstrate detection & containment controls (if available)

We appreciate a reply within 4 hours due to downstream processing.

Thanks,
Alice Burns
FinPlatform Security
security@finplatform.com

From: diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Elevated auth failures — evidence collection plan

Quick update from infra: I ran the process snapshot and correlated service logs. Findings so far:
- The svc-ingest-prod principal had 142 failed token refresh attempts between 2026-06-14 22:08:00 UTC and 2026-06-15 00:45:00 UTC, followed by successful requests starting at 2026-06-15 00:46:12 UTC.
- No code changes were deployed to the production ingress in that window (confirmed via deployment history). Canary rollout at 21:50 UTC did not include this principal.
- Network flows show a burst of retries from three ephemeral IPs; those IPs are new to our allowlist. We're exporting full pcap for the window to the secure bucket.

I'm continuing forensic capture and will include checksums for all artifacts in the bundle. ETA for full bundle: 4 hours. If FinPlatform needs immediate evidence, we can provide the access CSV and a timeline now (I recommend keeping the integration throttled).

Diego Fernandez
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: security@finplatform.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0400
Subject: Final evidence package and next steps — svc-ingest-prod event (IR-20260615)


Alice,

Thank you for your patience. Attached is the consolidated evidence package and explanatory statement for the elevated auth event. We have also populated a SIG control mapping that highlights our detection and containment controls relevant to the observed behavior. Summary below.

Summary (concise):
- Incident window: 2026-06-14 22:08 UTC — 2026-06-15 00:46 UTC
- Observed: high rate of failed token refreshes from svc-ingest-prod, followed by successful requests as retries continued; three ephemeral IPs observed initiating retries
- Root-cause hypothesis: unauthorized retry activity against a production service principal; not caused by our scheduled canary rollout (no deployment overlap). Further forensic work ongoing.
- Actions taken: throttled the integration, rotated service principal credentials for svc-ingest-prod, exported network flows and process snapshots, and initiated checksumed evidence bundle.

Artifacts attached (and in secure share):
- ir_evidence_bundle_v1.zip (contains access logs, pcap, process snapshots, checksums)
- access_logs_20260615.csv (CSV extract requested)
- sig_response_v1.xlsx (SIG mapping + SOC 2 control notes)

Links: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/FinPlatform/IRP-Evidence-20260615
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DEAL-8421

Next steps we propose:
1) FinPlatform to confirm whether you want the integration re-enabled after credential rotation (recommended waiting period: 24 hours).
2) We will share a formal postmortem and remediation plan once forensics complete (target: 2026-06-19).
3) If FinPlatform requests, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through with our security ops and infra teams — propose Wed 2026-06-17 14:00 UTC or Thu 2026-06-18 09:00 UTC.

If you need additional artifacts (full CloudTrail-style exports, longer retention logs) let us know and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
